content.page_title: Biomarkers and prognostic markers in acute pulmonary embolism (PE)
content.summary: Elevated cardiac biomarkers on admission are associated with worse prognosis in acute PE. Cardiac troponins, heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), and natriuretic peptides (BNP and NT-proBNP) provide prognostic information and can help stratify risk when combined with clinical and imaging findings.

biomarkers.name: Cardiac troponin I or T (cTnI/cTnT)
biomarkers.description: Cardiac troponin I or T elevation is defined as concentrations above assay-dependent normal limits. High-sensitivity assays detect more elevations.
biomarkers.prevalence_on_admission: Approximately 30% (conventional assays) to 60% (high-sensitivity assays) of patients with acute PE have elevated cardiac troponin.
prognostic_associations: Meta-analysis: increased risk of mortality (overall unselected patients OR ≈5.2, 95% CI ~3.3–8.4).
In haemodynamically stable patients at presentation: OR ≈5.9 (95% CI ~2.7–13.0).
biomarkers.diagnostic_performance_notes: On their own troponins have relatively low specificity and positive predictive value for early mortality in normotensive patients, but when combined with clinical/imaging data they improve risk identification and stratification.
cutoffs_and_predictive_values: High-sensitivity troponin T <14 pg/mL had a negative predictive value of ~98% for excluding an adverse in-hospital clinical outcome in a cohort of 526 normotensive patients.
Age-adjusted high-sensitivity troponin T cut-offs mentioned: ~14 pg/mL for patients aged <75 years and ~45 pg/mL for those ≥75 years (reported to improve negative predictive value).

biomarkers.name: Heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP)
biomarkers.description: An early and sensitive marker of myocardial injury that provides prognostic information in acute PE.
biomarkers.evidence: Meta-analysis of 1680 patients with PE evaluated H-FABP concentrations.
prognostic_associations: H-FABP concentrations >6 ng/mL were associated with increased risk of adverse short-term outcome (OR ≈17.7, 95% CI ~6.0–51.9).
Associated with increased all-cause mortality (OR ≈32.9, 95% CI ~8.8–123.2).

biomarkers.name: B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP)
biomarkers.description: Plasma natriuretic peptides are released with RV pressure overload and myocardial stretch; reflect severity of RV dysfunction and haemodynamic compromise in acute PE.
biomarkers.prevalence_on_admission: Meta-analysis: 51% of 1132 unselected patients with acute PE had elevated BNP or NT-proBNP on admission.
prognostic_associations: Patients with elevated natriuretic peptides had ~10% risk of early death (95% CI reported) and ~23% risk of an adverse clinical outcome (95% CI reported).
biomarkers.diagnostic_performance_notes: Similar to troponins, elevated BNP/NT-proBNP have low specificity and positive predictive value for early mortality in normotensive patients, but low levels can exclude unfavourable early outcomes (high sensitivity, high negative predictive value).
cutoffs_and_use: An NT-proBNP cut-off value <500 pg/mL was used in a multicentre management study to select patients for home treatment.

clinical_implications: Elevated cardiac biomarkers on admission identify patients at increased risk and can inform prognostic stratification when combined with clinical and imaging data.
High-sensitivity assays increase detection of troponin elevations and provide strong negative predictive value at low values.
Specific numeric cut-offs (e.g., hs-cTnT 14 pg/mL, age-adjusted thresholds, H-FABP >6 ng/mL, NT-proBNP <500 pg/mL for selecting low-risk outpatient management) are reported in the guideline text.
